hints: You can move from mountain a to mountain b only when a is taller than b and every mountain between them is lower than a.
For each mountain, find the nearest mountain of equal or greater height on its left and right; these are barriers.
Process mountains by increasing height; a valid jump lands on a strictly lower mountain inside the barrier interval, so query the best route there.
analogy: A tall mountain can see across a valley until an equally tall or taller mountain blocks the view.
correctness: The barrier interval contains exactly mountains visible from i; only lower heights have already been inserted, enforcing the strict taller-than condition. The range maximum chooses the best next mountain route.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
algorithm: Find nearest mountains of height >=h[i] on both sides with monotonic stacks. These are visibility barriers. Process mountains in increasing height batches; for i query the segment-tree maximum dp among indices strictly between its barriers, set dp[i]=1+max(0,that maximum), then insert all dp values in the batch. Equal heights cannot transition to one another.
example: For heights [3,1,2], the route 3->2->1 is valid: each move goes to a shorter mountain with every intervening mountain lower than the current one. The longest route has length 3.
